removed: time.sleep(1) inside the injected controller sleep hook
change.added: ModelDatetime injected into pipeline, scheduler, runtime and controller_worker modules; a stamp clock advances exactly 1 second per controller sleep so persisted run timestamps are ordered by tick, not wall time. Anchor is read once at test start.
kept_assertions: continuation pause on every earlier tick
change.residual_real_wait: time.sleep(0.002) in the fake transport read only forces thread overlap for the concurrency-peak assertion; it does not take part in deciding which tick completes delivery.

cause_analysis.mechanism: main() picks sleep_seconds = min(interval, CONTINUATION_PAUSE_SECONDS) only when run_controller_tick returns continuation_pending, which select_collector_pull_connectors derives from persisted fetch_state plus freshness.latest_run/is_due/staleness. Those use second-resolution timestamps from pipeline.utc_now_iso and scheduler._utc_now (datetime.now, microsecond=0) and are compared against real now (e.g. the 300s captured_at check and staleness<=interval check in controller_worker). The old test only separated ticks with a real 1s sleep, so which tick saw delivery done and which sleep value (1 continuation vs 60 interval, or 60 after a failed tick) it got depended on wall-clock second boundaries and runner speed.
cause_analysis.classification: test-only race: the production controller is a pure function of persisted state plus now; the test coupled real seconds to tick ordering. No production change made.
cause_analysis.reproduction_note: The original test was run 2 times under 8 busy workers on a 12-core host and passed both (a third run hit my 120s timeout); the failure was not reproduced locally, so the mechanism above is derived from code reading, not observed.
cause_analysis.residual_finding: Low-severity observation only: continuation/freshness decisions rely on second-resolution timestamps, so two runs in one second tie in _run_effective_at ordering. Not changed here (production out of scope).

verification.contention: 8 busy-loop python processes on a 12-core host
